newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia meat inspection fees to rise 13 pct-govt.
newsitem.headline: Australia meat inspection fees to rise 13 pct-govt.

text.p: Australian meat inspection costs would rise by 13 percent in aggregate under new pricing arrangements for the Australian Quarantine and Inspection Service (AQIS), the Minister for Primary Industries and Energy, John Anderson, said on Tuesday.
Concern raised that inspection costs would rise by up to 300 percent and that final decisions had been made on fees were incorrect, he said in a statement.
The total cost of AQIS services to the red meat sector had fallen to A$75.9 million in 1996/97 from A$84.1 million in 1995/96, he said.
It was proposed that the largest component of AQIS' fee structure, the annual inspection charge, would increase by only 3.7 percent, he said.
Overall, charges would increase by 13 percent to achieve full cost recovery, he said.

Anderson was responding to concern raised by Australia's meat industry that its international competitiveness would be affected by increased fees of up to 300 percent because of a decision by the government to charge the industry fully for AQIS operations.
